title: Failure bound for a scheduled estimator
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $S\subseteq J$. Write $W_f(J,S)$ for the restricted Fourier weight: the sum of squared Fourier coefficients at frequencies formed by adjoining to $S$ any subset of coordinates outside $J$. For real $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, there are rationals $\varepsilon',\delta'\in(0,\tfrac12]$, each strictly between half of the minimum of its corresponding parameter and $\tfrac12$, such that the scheduled estimator with parameters $\varepsilon',\delta'$ has probability at most $\delta$ of returning an estimate whose absolute error in estimating $W_f(J,S)$ is at least $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: The target is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a subset of the coordinates and $S$ is a subset of $J$
$\varepsilon'$ and $\delta'$ are positive rationals at most $1/2$, each greater than half the minimum of its corresponding real parameter and $1/2$, and each less than that minimum
